HOW MOVEMENT IS AUTHORISED
A plan proposes.
A permit authorises movement.

The planner suggests a move. Separate safety checks decide whether it may proceed. The robot controller then checks a signed permit: a permission for that specific move. STOP can always be requested without a movement permit.

01 / INTELLIGENCE
Perceive & plan

Use the map and current observations to propose a route. AI integrations require setup; a built-in planner provides a fallback.

A proposed move still needs permission
↓
02 / INDEPENDENT AUTHORITY
Verify every move

Check current conditions, hazards along the route, active safety rules, the mission and any stop controls.

SIGNED PERMISSION / ONE USE / SHORT LIFETIME / ONE EXACT MOVE
↓
03 / ROBOT CONTROLLER
Accept or refuse the move

The simulator controller independently validates the permit, then records the outcome. STOP never requires a permit.

Recorded robot updates support the audit history and checked learning
PERMISSION IS CHECKED TWICE
The AI proposes.
The controller checks.

A separate service issues a signed permit for one approved move. The controller checks that it is current, unchanged and unused before accepting it.

An expired or reused permit is refused. After an interruption, the system checks actual progress before continuing. STOP does not need a movement permit.

See safety, permits and operator review ↗

Understanding the current scope is part of trusting the platform. The current fleet has two mobile carriers and one humanoid navigator. All three support simulated navigation, stopping and waiting; physical manipulation and balancing are outside this scope.

Available in the simulator

Mission workflows, movement permits, stops, environment revalidation, learned routing, evidence, recovery and mixed-fleet navigation have documented test coverage.

Configuration or validation needed

Model planning, vision, voice, external lookup and tracing paths depend on suitable credentials, services and live validation. Operator review and replan-and-hold are available; approvals cannot override hard safety limits.

Not yet delivered

Physical humanoid manipulation and balancing, cross-platform skill transfer, enforced role-specific task eligibility and multi-site failover are outside current implementation.

pages.visible_text:
GOVERNANCE
The rules every move must pass

Eleven deterministic policies judge every proposal before the robot moves. The rules change only through a governed workflow; the planner learns from the gate, the gate does not drift.

Policies
Rules in force
Learning & task focus
Test a move or plan
WHERE THE ROBOT MAY GO
GEOFENCE_01
HIGH
Geofence enforcement

Deny actions if robot or destination is outside the allowed operating area.

When Robot position or destination outside boundary
Then STOP
min_x=0
max_x=40
min_y=0
max_y=25
PATH_CLEARANCE_07
HIGH
Path clearance

Deny a move whose straight path runs through permanent racking, so the robot replans along the aisles before it starts instead of being stopped when already close.

When Straight path to the target passes within 0.2 m of racking (robot body)
Then REPLAN
robot_radius_m=0.4
path_margin_m=0.6
OBSTACLE_CLEARANCE_03
HIGH
Obstacle clearance

Deny motion if nearest obstacle is below the minimum clearance distance.

When Obstacle distance < 0.5m
Then REPLAN
min_clearance_m=0.5
PEOPLE AND VEHICLES
HUMAN_PROXIMITY_02
HIGH
Human proximity enforcement

Enforce SLOW when a human or worker is within the slow radius, STOP within the stop radius.

When Human/worker within proximity radius
Then STOP if < 1m, SLOW if < 3m
slow_radius_m=3
stop_radius_m=1
max_speed_near_human_ms=0.4
HUMAN_CLEARANCE_02
HIGH
Human confidence speed check

Deny unsafe speed when a human is detected with high confidence and speed exceeds safe limit.

When Human detected (conf >= 0.65) and speed too high
Then SLOW
min_confidence=0.65
max_speed_near_human_ms=0.4
WORKER_PROXIMITY_06
HIGH
Walking worker proximity

Enforce SLOW/STOP when walking warehouse workers (separate from primary human detection) are within proximity radius.

When Walking worker within proximity radius
Then STOP if < 1m, SLOW if < 3m
slow_radius_m=3
stop_radius_m=1
UNCERTAINTY_04
MEDIUM
Perception uncertainty gate

Flag risky actions when human detection confidence is below the threshold.

When Human detected but confidence < 65%
Then SLOW + operator review
min_human_confidence=0.65
min_confidence_for_move=0.55
SPEED AND HAZARDS
SAFE_SPEED_01
HIGH
Zone speed limit

Enforce maximum speed per zone type. Aisle, corridor, and loading bay each have distinct limits.

When Proposed speed exceeds zone limit
Then SLOW
aisle_limit_ms=0.5
corridor_limit_ms=0.7
loading_bay_limit_ms=0.4
HAZARD_EXCLUSION_08
HIGH
Hazard exclusion zone

Deny a move that would enter or cross a temporary exclusion zone round a hazard such as a spill. Every spill gets a baseline zone at once; corroborated guidance from authoritative sources (via Tavily, screened as untrusted) can only enlarge it. A robot already inside may only back out, slowly.

When Path to the target passes within the zone radius, or the robot is inside and not leaving
Then REPLAN
baseline_radius_m=1.2
max_radius_m=6
corroborating_sources=2
HAZARD_SLOW_09
MEDIUM
Hazard slow zone

Cap speed near a hazard zone. Limits come from reviewed per-hazard rules (0.2 to 0.3 m/s), never from outside text.

When Robot or path within the slow radius above the zone's speed cap
Then SLOW
max_speed_range=0.1 to 0.3
ESCALATION
HITL_05
HIGH
Human-in-the-loop trigger

Escalate to operator review when aggregate risk score exceeds the threshold.

When Risk score >= 0.75
Then NEEDS_REVIEW (operator escalation)
risk_threshold=0.75
